{{Current events|year=2026|month=06|day=20|content=

<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[2026 Iran war]]
***[[2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis]]
****[[Operation Urja Suraksha]]
*****[[Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways#Cabinet Ministers|Indian shipping minister]] [[Sarbananda Sonowal]] says that three Indian [[oil tanker|oil tankers]], the ''Desh Vaibhav'', ''Desh Vibhor'', and ''Sanmar Herald'', have safely transited through the [[Strait of Hormuz]] and are on their way to [[India]]. [https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/us-iran-tensions-indian-oil-supertankers-safely-transit-strait-of-hormuz-desh-vibhor-desh-vaibhav-sanmar-herald-india-101782003882810.html (''Hindustan Times'')] [https://www.reuters.com/world/india/three-indian-flagged-oil-tankers-clear-strait-hormuz-minister-says-2026-06-20/ (Reuters)]
****The [[Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters|Iranian military command]] announces that the [[Strait of Hormuz]] is closed to [[Maritime shipping|traffic]] because of [[Israel]]'s violations of the [[Islamabad Memorandum]] [[ceasefire]] in [[Lebanon]]. The [[Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy]] warns ships to stay away from the strait. [https://aje.news/o3j66i?update=4681796 (Al Jazeera)] [https://aje.news/o3j66i?update=4681867 (Al Jazeera)]
****The [[United States Central Command]] says that 55 ships transporting more than 17 million barrels of oil and cargo have crossed the strait and that traffic on the chokepoint increased, rejecting Iran’s claims that the [[waterway]] is closed. [https://www.bbc.com/news/live/c9wq95g0lx2t (BBC News)] [https://shafaq.com/en/World/CENTCOM-17M-oil-barrels-moved-through-Hormuz (Shafaq)]
**[[Gaza war]]
***At least six people are killed in the [[Gaza Strip]], including two children, from Israeli strikes on a residential area. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/6/20/family-including-two-daughters-killed-in-israeli-strikes-on-gaza (Al Jazeera)]
***An Israeli airstrike kills [[Al Jazeera]] cameraman Ahmed Wishah. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/6/20/al-jazeera-cameraman-ahmad-wishah-killed-in-israeli-attack-in-gaza (Al Jazeera)]
**[[2026 Lebanon war]]
***[[Israel]]i [[airstrike]]s on southern Lebanon kill at least 32 people, including sixteen people in [[Nabatieh]] and two [[Lebanese Armed Forces|soldiers]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/6/20/us-envoy-headed-for-switzerland-israeli-strikes-on-lebanon-threaten-talks (Al Jazeera)]
***The [[Prime Minister's Office (Israel)|office]] of [[Prime Minister of Israel|Israeli prime minister]] [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] states that [[Israeli occupation of Southern Lebanon (2026)|Israeli troops will remain]] in [[southern Lebanon]] to protect [[Blue Line (withdrawal line)|Israel's northern border]] for as long as it is believed to be necessary. [https://aje.news/o3j66i?update=4682103 (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Kordofan campaign (2023–present)|Kordofan campaign]]
***The [[Sudanese Army]] says that they have launched drone strikes to foil preparations by [[Rapid Support Forces]] to launch new assaults on the [[North Kordofan]] [[Capital city|capital]] of [[El Obeid]] in [[Sudan]]. [https://sudantribune.com/article/315279 (''Sudan Tribune'')]
*[[Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]]
**Two [[roadside bomb]] explosions in [[Bannu District]], [[Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]], [[Pakistan]], kill at least seven people and injure three others. The second blast occurred as casualties from the first explosion were being transported for medical treatment. [https://globalnation.inquirer.net/327948/two-roadside-blasts-in-northwest-pakistan-kill-7-police (AFP via ''Philippine Daily Inquirer'')]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Turkey]] exports a warship to [[Romania]], a [[NATO]] and [[European Union]] member country, for the first time in its history. [https://www.trtworld.com/article/951a3f425290 (TRT World)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Three people are killed in a fire at a single-story [[pavilion]] in [[West London]], [[London]], [[England]]. [https://news.sky.com/story/white-city-three-people-killed-following-fire-in-west-london-13556237?dcmp=snt-sf-twitter (Sky News)]
*One person is killed when two [[freight train]]s [[traffic collision|collide]] and fall off of a bridge in [[Munich]], [[Bavaria]], [[Germany]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/one-dead-after-freight-trains-collide-munich-2026-06-20/ (Reuters)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2020–2026 H5N1 outbreak]]
**The [[Australian Government]] confirms the first detection of the [[avian influenza]] [[Influenza A virus subtype H5N1|subtype H5N1]] in [[Australia|the country]] after identifying the virus in a wild [[seabird]] in [[Western Australia]]. The strain has now been recorded on every continent. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260620-australia-detects-first-case-of-contagious-h5-bird-flu (AFP via France 24)]
*[[2026 European heatwaves]]
**[[Météo-France]] places 35 [[Departments of France|departments]], including [[Paris]], under red [[heat wave]] alert as high temperatures persist [[France|nationwide]]. Authorities also prohibit public [[Alcohol in France|alcohol consumption]] during [[Fête de la Musique]] events in affected areas and implement measures to reduce pressure on [[Emergency medical services in France|emergency services]]. [https://www.omanobserver.om/article/1191536/world/europe/red-heat-alert-issued-for-third-of-france (AFP via ''Oman Observer'')]
*[[Whaling in Iceland]]
**A commercial [[whaling]] vessel departs from [[Reykjavík]], marking the resumption of [[Iceland]]'s whale hunt after a two-year suspension. The season proceeds under reduced catch recommendations issued by the country's Marine and Freshwater Research Institute. [https://www.nzherald.co.nz/world/iceland-resumes-whale-hunting-after-two-year-hiatus-amid-protest/D4QVPHBLJBC6FCTT32OT3YCM54/ (AFP via ''New Zealand Herald'')]
*In a major recovery from climate-related disaster, thousands of [[flamingo]] eggs hatched at [[Lake Tuz]] in [[Turkey]]. [https://www.goodnewsnetwork.org/thousands-of-flamingo-chicks-hatch-in-major-comeback-after-climate-disaster/ (Good News Network)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Koldo Case]]
**A [[Spain|Spanish]] [[Judiciary of Spain|court]] orders [[Begoña Gómez]], the wife of [[Prime Minister of Spain|prime minister]] [[Pedro Sánchez]], to stand trial on [[Corruption in Spain|corruption]]-related charges, confiscates her [[Spanish passport|passport]], and restricts her international travel pending proceedings. [https://www.reuters.com/world/spanish-pms-wife-must-stand-trial-corruption-charges-judge-rules-2026-06-20/ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2026 Bolivian protests]]
**[[Bolivia]]n [[President of Bolivia|president]] [[Rodrigo Paz]] declares a [[state of emergency]], deploying [[Armed Forces of Bolivia|the military]] to clear the [[road blockade]]s. [https://www.cnn.com/2026/06/20/americas/bolivia-president-state-of-emergency-intl-hnk (CNN)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/bolivias-paz-declares-state-emergency-over-blockade-crisis-2026-06-20/ (Reuters)]
*Members of [[Mexico]]'s [[Coordinadora Nacional de Trabajadores de la Educación]] end a 20-day [[Strike action|strike]] over wages and [[Pensions in Mexico|pensions]]. The protests included demonstrations and [[road blockade]]s in [[Mexico City]], some of which targeted areas associated with the [[2026 FIFA World Cup|FIFA World Cup]]. [https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/06/21/world/mexican-teachers-end-strike-after-20-days/2369539 (AFP via ''The Manila Times'')]

'''Sports'''
*[[2026 FIFA World Cup]]
**[[Curaçao at the FIFA World Cup]]
***In [[association football]], [[FIFA World Cup]] debutants [[Curaçao national football team|Curaçao]], the smallest [[Curaçao|nation]] by population to play at the World Cup, earn their first-ever [[Three points for a win|point]] at the tournament after drawing 0–0 against [[Ecuador national football team|Ecuador]] in the [[2026 FIFA World Cup Group E|group stage]]. [https://www.philstar.com/sports/2026/06/21/2536801/room-heroics-earn-curacao-world-cup-point-against-ecuador (AFP via ''The Philippine Star'')]
**[[Tunisia v Japan (2026 FIFA World Cup)]]
***The 1,000th FIFA World Cup match is held at the [[Estadio BBVA]] in [[Monterrey]], [[Mexico]], with [[Japan national football team|Japan]] defeating [[Tunisia national football team|Tunisia]] 4–0 in the [[2026 FIFA World Cup Group F|group stage]]. [https://www.japantimes.co.jp/sports/2026/06/21/soccer/japan-routs-tunisia-world-cup/ (''Japan Times'')] [https://www.rte.ie/sport/world-cup-2026/2026/0620/1579440-rampant-japan-tear-tunisia-asunder-in-monterrey/ (RTÉ)]
